---
title: "Visualizing the Bias–Variance Tradeoff"
author: "Anthony Morciglio"
date: "11/17/2025"
output: html_document
---

## Introduction

This RMarkdown document illustrates the **Bias–Variance Tradeoff** using simulated data.
We generate a nonlinear true function and fit polynomial regression models of increasing 
complexity. For each model, we estimate:

- **Bias²**  
- **Variance**  
- **Total Error = Bias² + Variance**

Finally, we visualize how model complexity impacts the three components.

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

# ---------------------------------------------------
# 1. Generate the "true" underlying function
# ---------------------------------------------------
true_f <- function(x) sin(2*pi*x)   # Nonlinear true function
n <- 50
x_vals <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
true_y <- true_f(x_vals)

# ---------------------------------------------------
# 2. Simulation settings
# ---------------------------------------------------
num_sims <- 200           # Number of simulated datasets
poly_degrees <- 1:12      # Model complexity

# Storage for results
results <- data.frame(
  degree = integer(),
  bias2 = numeric(),
  variance = numeric(),
  total_error = numeric()
)

# ---------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute Bias^2, Variance, and Total Error
# ---------------------------------------------------
for (deg in poly_degrees) {
  
  preds <- matrix(0, nrow=num_sims, ncol=n)
  
  for (i in 1:num_sims) {
    y_noise <- true_y + rnorm(n, sd=0.3)
    model <- lm(y_noise ~ poly(x_vals, degree=deg, raw=TRUE))
    preds[i, ] <- predict(model)
  }
  
  mean_preds <- colMeans(preds)
  
  bias2 <- mean((mean_preds - true_y)^2)
  variance <- mean(apply(preds, 2, var))
  total_error <- bias2 + variance
  
  results <- rbind(results,
                   data.frame(
                     degree = deg,
                     bias2 = bias2,
                     variance = variance,
                     total_error = total_error))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------
# 4. Plot the Bias–Variance tradeoff
# ---------------------------------------------------

results_long <- results %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c("bias2","variance","total_error"),
                      names_to = "type", values_to = "value")

ggplot(results_long, aes(x = degree, y = value, color = type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Bias–Variance Tradeoff",
       x = "Model Complexity (Polynomial Degree)",
       y = "Error",
       color = "Component") +
  theme_minimal()

# ---------------------------------------------------
# 5. Visualize underfitting vs overfitting
# ---------------------------------------------------

make_plot <- function(deg){
  y_noise <- true_y + rnorm(n, sd=0.3)
  model <- lm(y_noise ~ poly(x_vals, degree=deg, raw=TRUE))
  
  df_plot <- data.frame(
    x = x_vals,
    true = true_y,
    fitted = predict(model)
  )
  
  ggplot(df_plot, aes(x)) +
    geom_line(aes(y=true), color="black", size=1.2) +
    geom_line(aes(y=fitted), color="blue", size=1) +
    labs(title = paste("Model Fit: Polynomial Degree =", deg),
         y = "y") +
    theme_minimal()
}

# Show low-complexity (underfit), medium, and high-complexity (overfit)
make_plot(1)
make_plot(5)
make_plot(12)

```
